docs.title: Clerk CLI
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: The Clerk CLI is a command-line tool for you and your agents to set up and manage Clerk authentication directly from the terminal. It supports 10+ frameworks.

docs.title: Installation
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Install the CLI globally, or run it directly without installing using npx clerk or bunx clerk.

docs.title: Get started
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: This command auto-detects your framework, installs the appropriate Clerk SDK, and applies framework-specific setup such as auth pages, middleware, and providers. If you're authenticated with clerk auth login, it also links your project to a Clerk application and pulls your…

docs.snippet: - **Set up authentication** — clerk init detects your framework, installs the SDK, and scaffolds your project with Clerk's authentication setup. - **Manage your account and project link** — clerk auth login and clerk auth logout manage your CLI session, clerk whoami shows the…

docs.title: Which frameworks are supported?
docs.heading_path: Clerk CLI > Frequently asked questions (FAQ) > Which frameworks are supported?
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: The CLI supports frameworks such as Next.js, React, Vue, Nuxt, Astro, React Router, TanStack Start, and more. Some frameworks like Expo, Express, and Fastify are supported for SDK installation but don't yet include full scaffolding. Run clerk init --help for the current list.

docs.title: Maintenance Mode
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Once or twice per year, Clerk undergoes maintenance on its infrastructure and enters **Maintenance Mode**. During this time, users who are already signed in will not be signed out, and will continue to have access to your app. However, new sign-ups, sign-ins and user mutations…

docs.title: Production instances
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Mutation methods (POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE) will be rejected with a SystemUnderMaintenance error. This includes all new sign-ups and sign-ins.

docs.title: API errors
docs.heading_path: Maintenance Mode > Production instances > API errors
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: All mutations from both the Frontend API and the Backend API will return the following SystemUnderMaintenance error.

docs.title: UI components
docs.heading_path: Maintenance Mode > Production instances > UI components
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: During **Maintenance Mode**, Clerk's UI components will display the following error for sign-ins, sign-ups, and all mutations to user and org data.

docs.title: Development instances
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: For development instances, all requests will return a SystemUnderMaintenance error, and the instance will be completely unavailable.

docs.title: Ways to implement Clerk
docs.heading_path: Core concepts > Ways to implement Clerk
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Clerk provides three ways to integrate authentication into your application, depending on the level of control and customization you need:

docs.title: Configuring your application
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Configuring your application is done through the Clerk Dashboard. The Clerk Dashboard is where you, as the application owner, can manage your application's settings, users, and organizations.

docs.title: Session token
docs.heading_path: Core concepts > Building your application > Session token
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: When a user is authenticated in your application, Clerk generates a short-lived session token that you can use to authenticate requests to your backend. This token is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that contains information about the user and their session.

docs.title: Key Clerk objects
docs.heading_path: Core concepts > Building your application > Key Clerk objects
docs.attribution: © Clerk — via llms.txt agent interface, via documesh
docs.snippet: Clerk's SDKs are built on top of many key objects, like the Clerk, User, and Session objects. As you're building your application, you'll likely interact with these objects, either directly or through hooks and helpers. Refer to the reference docs for more information.
